answer: One concrete sybil-resistance mechanism is a proof-of-identity stake: each agent must lock a scarce on-chain credential whose pigment is unique to a verified operator, and every new agent begins its voyage with a hollow reputation ledger. Duplicate identities are detected by credential collision, so an attacker must acquire and bond a fresh costly credential per fake agent, making mass sybils economically unviable.
